pr.title: Add install.sh and field upgrade: install a checkout and keep it current (install.md chunk 1)
pr.head: bc3b54656f0e0a52e6fd75e94728ba99fddf10ac

summary: Field is installed from a git checkout, and it has four pieces that each go stale on their own. The field command is TypeScript built into dist/. The field ui client is a React app built into ui/dist, and it bundles some of the CLI's code. The audio daemon field-audiod is a C++ binary built with CMake and JUCE. The model workers are Python environments that uv manages. Until this change, installing meant several pnpm commands run inside the checkout, and nothing said which piece was out of date after a git pull.

This pull request adds install.sh at the repository root. It installs the checkout it sits in: it builds the CLI and the UI and links field onto your PATH through pnpm, builds the daemon, and re-syncs the worker environments someone already set up. It never sets up a new worker, because that starts a download of several gigabytes. field upgrade [target] runs the same script from any directory, and field upgrade status compares each piece with its source and names the command that fixes it. The installer checks every prerequisite a target needs before it changes anything, and it never pulls or switches branches, because the checkout may hold work in progress.

Three smaller changes support it. field setup gains --existing and --check, so the CLI, which owns the list of workers, says which are set up. The CLI's error messages take their remedies from src/remedies.ts, which names field upgrade cli or field upgrade audiod rather than a pnpm script that does not exist inside a song project. And pnpm gen:limits stops rewriting an unchanged C++ header, which made the daemon look stale after every test run. On Windows the installer does not run, so field upgrade refuses there, and each remedy names the pnpm script to run in the checkout.

cards.title: What each target runs
cards.html:
TargetRuns
clipnpm install --frozen-lockfile, pnpm run build, pnpm run build:ui, then pnpm add -g <checkout> unless pnpm's global field already links this checkout
audioda CMake 3.24 or newer check, pnpm run build:native, then touch the binary so audiod-stale clears
workersfield setup --existing from the checkout's dist/
all (default)cli, audiod, then workers
statusOne row per fact, changing nothing

Each target checks every prerequisite it needs before its first command. Every target except status ends by fetching the checkout's upstream and warning when the branch is behind it.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Checkout: the git clone of Field that install.sh sits in, and the code that field runs.
  • The link: pnpm's global node_modules/field, a symlink into the checkout that pnpm add -g <checkout> creates. A new build takes effect without relinking.
  • Build stamp: dist/build-info.json, which pnpm build writes with the commit it built and the number of uncommitted files it saw.
  • Set up: a worker whose console script is installed in python/<worker>/.venv, the test field generate applies before starting one.
  • Remedy: the command an error message tells you to run. src/remedies.ts holds them.
  • Upstream: the remote branch that the checkout's branch tracks, @{upstream} in git.

cards.html:

groups.title: The installer: install.sh
groups.kicker: One bash script installs the checkout it sits in, one target at a time, and reports what is out of date.
intro: install.sh treats itself as a checkout's installer when src/cli.ts sits beside it. Piped from curl, bash reads it from stdin with nothing beside it, and it says to clone instead. A later chunk adds release installs for that case. It is written for bash 3.2, the version macOS ships, and takes one target, all when given none.

Each target checks every prerequisite it needs before its first command: Node 24 or newer, pnpm, pnpm's global bin directory on PATH unless field already links this checkout, and CMake 3.24 or newer for audiod and all. A missing or old one stops the installer with exit status 69 and nothing changed. A C++ compiler and the Linux development headers are not checked. The daemon build reports them.

The cli target keeps the install shape the README already documented. pnpm add -g <checkout> makes pnpm's global field a symlink into the checkout. To tell which checkout pnpm links, linked_checkout reads pnpm ls -g --json and resolves the path it names. A link that already points here is left alone, and one that points at another checkout moves, with a moved row naming both. The cli target also builds the UI every time, because field ui serves ui/dist and that bundle imports code from src/.
status compares each piece with its source:

• Checkout: commits in HEAD..@{upstream} and @{upstream}..HEAD after a fetch, which FIELD_OFFLINE=1 skips. A branch behind its upstream warns, and one only ahead reports repo-ahead.
  • CLI: the build stamp's commit and dirty-file count against the checkout's, the comparison field --version already makes.
  • UI: the modification time of ui/dist/index.html, which Vite rewrites on every build, against every tracked file under ui/ and src/ except tests, and pnpm-lock.yaml.
  • Daemon: the binary's modification time against every tracked file under native/audiod. The installer touches the binary after each build, because CMake relinks it only when its own inputs change.
  • Workers: the rows field setup --check prints, passed through.

checks.text: Exit statuses: 69 for a missing prerequisite, 64 for an unknown target, and 1 when the daemon build fails. Messages name field upgrade <target> as the way back when pnpm's field links this checkout, and the script's own path otherwise (rerun).

files.note: The whole installer: prerequisite checks, the four install targets, and the status rows.

checks.text: The JSON shape linked_checkout reads matches pnpm 11.15.1: pnpm ls -g --json lists dependencies.field.path as a node_modules/field path in the global directory, which pwd -P resolves to the linked checkout. Checked against a real listing.

The version check, run in the test sandbox with a stand-in cmake for each version. 3.22.1 and 3.23.5 exit 69 from all and audiod with nothing changed, and 3.24.0, 3.24.0-rc1, 4.0.0, 10.1, and real cmake --version output pass. An unreadable version also exits 69, and a cmake that exits non-zero reads as missing.

The UI builds after the CLI and before the link, so a UI that fails to build stops the target before field is linked. pnpm run build:ui took about two seconds in a scratch worktree and left the checkout clean, since dist/ is ignored.
Moving the link works with the real pnpm 11.15.1. In a throwaway PNPM_HOME, pnpm add -g of a second package named field replaced the first, and pnpm ls -g --json then named the new path.

This touch is what clears audiod-stale. In the test sandbox with the real CMake on a two-target project, an edit to the other target's source left field-audiod unlinked by the rebuild. status then printed audiod-current, and with this line removed it still printed audiod-stale.
GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and the 15-second low-speed limit bound a stalled HTTPS fetch. Neither applies to an SSH remote.

The UI row needs no touch, unlike the daemon's: Vite rewrites index.html on every build, so field upgrade cli always clears ui-stale. The sandbox showed the row turn current after install.sh cli. It counts every file under src/, so an edit to code the UI does not import also reads as stale.

Every target checks before its first command. In the test sandbox, all without cmake, without the global bin directory on PATH, without a global bin directory, or with Node 22, and audiod without cmake, each exit 69 with nothing installed, built, or linked.

groups.title: Workers: field setup --existing and --check
groups.kicker: The CLI, which owns the list of workers, says which are set up and whether each is current.
intro: Field's model workers are Python packages under python/<worker>/, each with an environment in .venv that uv manages. Setting one up is explicit, because the first field generate of each kind downloads that model's weights: about 10 GB for ACE-Step and 2 GB for Chatterbox. A worker counts as set up when its console script is installed in .venv/bin. A .venv alone does not count, because a dev-only uv sync creates one with no worker in it.

--existing re-syncs only the workers already set up, and prints a skipping line for each of the others. --check prints one row per worker in the installer's row format and changes nothing. It exits 1 only when a worker someone set up is out of date, or uv is missing, because a worker nobody set up is not a problem.

checks.text: partitionExisting decides with workerScriptInstalled, the same check probeEnvironment makes before field generate starts a worker. src/workers/setup.test.ts covers the installed and dev-only layouts and passed at this head.

checkWorkers pads each label to 14 characters to match row in install.sh, which passes these rows through and marks worker-stale and worker-no-uv as warnings. The probe it calls runs only uv --version and uv sync --check --locked, which change nothing.

groups.title: field upgrade and the command surface
groups.kicker: A small command that finds the install.sh beside its own package and hands it the target.
intro: Because field is a pnpm link, Node loads it from the checkout itself. So installerPath() finds install.sh two directories above dist/commands/upgrade.js, with no record of where Field was installed from. upgrade prints the command it runs, runs it through bash rather than the script's execute bit, and returns the script's exit status.
On Windows the installer does not run, so field upgrade refuses and names the steps to run in the checkout instead. src/cli.ts registers the command and the two new field setup options.

files.note: The whole command: refuse on Windows, find the installer, print the command, run it through bash, and return its status.

checks.text: The Windows refusal comes first, so field upgrade status refuses there too.

files.note: Registers field upgrade and the --existing and --check options on field setup, and takes BUILD_DAEMON from src/remedies.ts for three field play messages.

checks.text: --check with --existing is refused, since one reports and the other syncs.

groups.title: Remedies name field upgrade
groups.kicker: src/remedies.ts gives every message that needs a fix one command to name.
intro: Several messages tell you how to fix a missing or stale build: eight for the daemon, two in field --version for a stale CLI, and two in field ui for a missing client or app shell. They fire while you work in a song project, where the checkout's pnpm scripts do not exist. Each now takes its command from src/remedies.ts.

• BUILD_DAEMON is field upgrade audiod.
  • BUILD_CLI, BUILD_UI, and INSTALL_UI are all field upgrade cli, because that target installs the workspace, builds the CLI, and builds the UI.
  • On Windows, where field upgrade refuses, each names its pnpm script followed by "in the field checkout", outside a code span so the instruction does not read as part of the command.

files.note: New. The four remedies, each field upgrade <target>, or on Windows the pnpm script to run in the checkout.
A missing client names BUILD_UI, and a missing app shell names INSTALL_UI.

checks.text: field upgrade cli fixes both cases. The root pnpm install put ui/node_modules/electron/cli.js in place, which is the file this command checks for before it starts the app shell, and build:ui writes ui/dist/index.html, which it checks here.

files.note: A stale build names BUILD_CLI, and a daemon on the wrong protocol names BUILD_DAEMON.

groups.title: gen:limits writes the header only when it changes
groups.kicker: A generated header stops making the daemon look stale after every test run.
intro: native/audiod/src/plan-limits.h carries the zod schemas' limits into the daemon's C++, and src/schema/plan-limits.test.ts regenerates it on every pnpm test to prove it is in step. Rewriting identical bytes moved the file's modification time. That made the next daemon build recompile every file that includes the header, and made the new audiod-stale row fire after every test run.

files.note: Compares the new header with the file on disk and writes only when they differ.

checks.text: At this head, pnpm gen:limits printed is current and left the header's modification time unchanged, and src/schema/plan-limits.test.ts passed.

groups.title: Tests run the real script in a sandbox
groups.kicker: The installer's tests run install.sh under real bash with stand-ins for pnpm, cmake, and the CLI.
intro: src/install.test.ts runs the real install.sh with the machine's bash against a temporary clone that has its own upstream. pnpm and cmake are stand-ins that record their arguments, the CLI is a stand-in script, and PATH and HOME point only into the temporary directory, so the machine's real tools cannot answer in their place. src/commands/upgrade.test.ts runs bash against a stand-in installer. Both skip on Windows.

checks.text: At this head, pnpm typecheck was clean, and these files with the generate, plan-limits, and field ui tests passed: 7 files and 124 tests. On CI, linux passed. windows failed only in test files this pull request does not change, which also fail in main's own Windows runs.
The refusal tests assert that a failed check logs no install, build, or link at all, through changes.
The CMake version tests cover 3.22.1 refused and 4.0.0 accepted. The review also ran 3.23.5, 3.24.0, 3.24.0-rc1, 10.1, and unreadable output in the same sandbox.
The pnpm stand-in leaves an existing daemon alone, as CMake does after an edit to another target's source, so this test fails without the touch in install_audiod.

This test keeps CMAKE_MAJOR and CMAKE_MINOR in step with cmake_minimum_required. It passes, it fails when CMAKE_MINOR is set to 25, and it runs and passes on the Windows CI job, since it only reads files.

groups.title: Documentation
groups.kicker: A new install guide, and every install instruction now leads with ./install.sh.
intro: docs/install.md is new. It describes the prerequisites, what each target runs, the link, worker environments, every status row, and the manual steps on Windows. The README, the CLI manual, the architecture notes, the keys guide, and the example project's README now lead with ./install.sh and name field upgrade as the remedy.

files.note: The install guide: targets, the link, workers, and the status rows.

checks.text: The prerequisites paragraph now names what the installer checks, Node, pnpm, and CMake, and says the daemon build reports a missing compiler or headers after all has installed the CLI.
The UI row says outright that an edit to a src/ file the UI does not import also reads as stale.

files.note: The install section, the field setup options, the reference table, and FIELD_OFFLINE.
The field --version drift messages now name field upgrade cli.

groups.title: The install plan
groups.kicker: The new plan records chunk 1 as built and designs releases and the one-line install.
intro: docs/projects/install/readme.md is new at status: in-progress. §2 is the design this pull request builds, §3 sketches chunks 2 to 4, §4 records why each choice beat its alternatives, and §8 records what implementation settled and how it was verified.

§7 holds the open questions. Each must be answered or deferred to where it gets decided, because in-progress claims the plan is ready to execute. §7.1, the daemon binary's license, is deferred to before chunk 2, and it notes that JUCE 8.0.11 and later bundle the VST3 SDK under MIT, which would leave only JUCE's own terms to decide. §7.5 and the install.ps1 question in §7.6 go to chunk 3, and §8.3 defers the rest that gate chunks 2 to 4.

files.note: The plan, from the problem through chunk 1 as built.

checks.text: §2.2 lists what the installer checks before anything changes, now with CMake 3.24 or newer, and says the compiler and headers are left to the daemon build.
§4 records why the UI builds inside the cli target rather than a ui target of its own: one remedy, field upgrade cli, then covers both.

The JUCE claims check out. JUCE's change list gives "Updated the VST3 SDK to 3.8.0 (MIT license)" under 8.0.11 and 3.7.12 before it. All four LICENSE.txt files under VST3_SDK at JUCE's 8.0.11 tag are MIT, and so is the one at the SDK's v3.8.0_build_66 tag. The daemon sets no JUCE_ASIO, so the GPLv3 ASIO SDK stays out of it.
Chunk 3 owns the install.ps1 question, here and in §6, so every question in the plan is answered or deferred to a named chunk. project check passes.
